metadata.title: SC-ST-OBC लिस्ट में नई एंट्री | Classification of denotified tribes | Main Bhi Bharat
metadata.description:
For the first time, the Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI) and Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) have comprehensively classified 268 denotified, semi-nomadic, and nomadic tribes after a three-year study. The research has led to the recommendation of 179 communities for inclusion in the Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC) lists, ensuring them constitutional recognition and access to welfare programs. Among these, 85 communities are being classified for the first time.

The study also found that 63 previously unclassified communities are now “not traceable,” likely due to assimilation, migration, or name changes. These findings highlight the historical neglect and systemic marginalization faced by these tribes, many of whom were once stigmatized under colonial-era “criminal tribe” laws. This classification marks a crucial step in addressing their socio-economic disadvantages, preserving their cultural heritage, and ensuring their rightful place in India’s development framework.
